title: fix(plugin-grid,types): an import undo that leaves rows unreverted says so (objectui#13015)
body:
Fixes #13015
Clause-②: yes (narrowing) (`ImportJobUndoResult`, exported from `@object-ui/types`, gains the required `failures` member. The new `grid.import.undoPartial` count family widens `@object-ui/i18n`'s `TranslationKeys`, and `failures` is now required of a custom `DataSource`'s `undoImportJob` answer.)

## What this does

The undo route answers `200` with `success: false` and one `failures` entry per row a control refused. That shape landed in objectstack-ai/objectstack#24431, which objectui's pin `f4755a68a797` carries. The job stays undoable for exactly those rows. The wizard never read the answer.

- **The hook reads the answer.** `useImportJobUndo` (`packages/plugin-grid/src/ImportWizard.tsx`) now takes the result of `ds.undoImportJob(jobId)`. On `success: false` it hands the answer to the list that ran Undo. A throw is handed over as before. The object's readers still get `notifyDataChanged`, because a partial undo reverted the other rows.
- **Both lists draw it.** The History list and the cancelled-result screen render one shared `ImportUndoOutcomeNotice`. It shows:
  - how many rows were not undone (`failed`), and that undoing again retries only those rows (`grid.import.undoPartial`, a count family in all ten packs);
  - each refusal sentence the answer's `failures[].error` carries, the app's own words. Rows with the same sentence share one line, because one hook typically refuses many rows alike (an undoable job holds up to 5,000 rows). After ten distinct sentences the rest are counted with the existing `grid.import.moreErrors`.
- **Undo stays offered** after a partial undo, because the re-read job is still `undoable` and not `revertedAt`. That is correct per the contract, so the button is not hidden. Undoing again clears the notice as it starts.
- **A full undo is unchanged.** `success: true` shows nothing new and flips the row to "Undone" as before.
- **`ImportJobUndoResult` is bound to the spec.** It is now `UndoImportJobResponse` from `@objectstack/spec/api`, by reference, the way `ImportRowResult` and its siblings at the top of `packages/types/src/data.ts` already are. The hand-written copy it replaces said it mirrored the server and lacked `failures`; that drift is this card's defect.

### Bounded in-place fix in the same hook (named here, with evidence)

In the History list, a **thrown** undo also showed nothing. The hook wrote the message into the panel's `error` slot, then called the reload, and `load()` clears `error` as it starts, in the same tick. The partial notice would have been wiped the same way, so the undo outcome now has its own slot (`undoOutcome`), and the thrown message goes there too.

- Evidence: a one-off probe against the base file (`c2191654a`): render the History list, an undo that rejects with a sentence, wait for the reload, and assert the sentence is on screen. Result: `1 failed`, `expect(received).toBeInTheDocument()`. The probe was deleted, and the file was restored to HEAD (blob equal, `git diff HEAD` empty).
- The four conditions hold. It is the same defect class (an undo's outcome the user never sees, in the same list). It is mechanical (one state slot the reload does not touch). The file is under this claim. It adds no new gate surface. The committed pin is `History list: an undo that throws shows its message after the list reloads`.

## Premises measured (PM hypotheses)

- **H1 held.** At `c2191654a` the hook ran `await ds.undoImportJob(jobId); notifyDataChanged(...)` and its only error path was the `catch`. It had two callers: the History list and the cancelled-result screen.
- **H2 held, so the producer side does not move.** The server's route (objectstack `f4755a68a797`, `packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts`) answers a flat `res.json({ success, jobId, object, deleted, restored, failed, failures })`. The installed client at the pin (`node_modules/.cache/objectstack/client`, `18.0.0-next.5`) has `unwrapResponse` unwrap only a body that has `data`, and its `fetch` throws only on `!res.ok`. `@object-ui/data-objectstack`'s `undoImportJob` returns the client's answer unchanged. So `failures` already reached the wizard at runtime; only the type and the UI dropped it.
- **H3: derived, not hand-mirrored.** `check:spec-symbols` does not require it: the local name differs from the spec's, and the comment named no `@objectstack/spec` symbol. But the tree's convention (the header block of `packages/types/src/data.ts`, "Spec-owned names are bound here, not re-declared") and commandment #0 point the same way, and the hand copy is exactly what drifted. Reading `failures` through the spec makes `@object-ui/types` the first consumer of the release that first publishes it, so the floor moves (below).
- **H4 held.** After a partial undo, both lists re-read the job and it still offers Undo. The fix is the message, not hiding Undo.

## Spec floor

`@object-ui/types` moves `@objectstack/spec` from `^18.0.0-next.2` to `^18.0.0-next.5`.

- R = `18.0.0-next.5`, the first published release carrying `UndoImportJobResponseSchema.failures` (objectstack `adb7910f8`, PR objectstack-ai/objectstack#24431). The registry lists `18.0.0-next.0` to `18.0.0-next.3` and `18.0.0-next.5`; `18.0.0-next.4` was never published.
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor adb7910f8` against the `@objectstack/spec@18.0.0-next.5` tag commit gives exit 0. Against the `…next.3` tag commit it gives exit 1. The control leg (the `…next.2` tag commit against `…next.3`) gives exit 0, so the exit 1 is a real non-ancestor on that checkout.
- The packed tarballs agree: `failures: z.ZodArray` has 2 hits in next.5's `dist/api/index.d.mts` and 0 in next.2's.
- The lockfile does not move: the importer resolves the spec through the pin override (`file:../../.objectstack-pin/spec`).
- `@object-ui/plugin-grid` keeps its own floor. It reads `failures` only through `@object-ui/types`, and its artifact names no `UndoImportJobResponse`.
- Scoped `check:spec-floors` over `@object-ui/types`: **0 findings** at `^18.0.0-next.5`. The run also clears the two `floor-too-low` findings `@object-ui/types` had at next.2 (`checkPageMainRegionWidth`, `checkPageRecordBindingPlacement`); next.5's `dist/ui/index.d.mts` carries `checkPageMainRegionWidth` (1 hit, 0 in next.2). That is objectui#13065's subject; this PR closes no card but this one. The whole-repo run exits 1 only on 14 `no-artifact` findings for packages outside this branch's build closure.

## Tests

All runs below are at `13af833` (the source has not changed since `92728ce`).

- New file `packages/plugin-grid/src/ImportWizard.undoPartial-13015.test.tsx`, which drives the real wizard with a stubbed data source: 4 tests, `4 passed`.
  - History list, partial answer (`success: false`, `failed: 3`, three `failures` with two distinct sentences). It shows "3 rows were not undone. Undo again to retry only those rows.", lists both sentences once each, survives the reload, keeps Undo offered, and emits one data change.
  - History list: a second Undo answering in full clears the notice and shows "Undone".
  - History list: a thrown undo shows its message after the reload.
  - Cancelled-result screen, the same partial answer: count, both sentences and retry sentence shown, and Undo still offered, because the re-read job is undoable.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-grid/`: `Test Files 229 passed (229)`, `Tests 2077 passed (2077)`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/i18n/ packages/types/` (the ten-pack key parity, plural-category and count-family pins, plus the `types` suite): `Test Files 472 passed (472)`, `Tests 11870 passed | 13 skipped (11883)`. The skips are the env-gated `describe.runIf(DRIVEN)` timezone suites, the only conditional markers in those two packages.

### Ablations (one-off, through `ablation-replace.mjs`, each restored to HEAD with blob equality and an empty `git diff HEAD`)

The subject resolves to `packages/plugin-grid/src` (a relative import), and `@object-ui/types` resolves to `src` through the root vitest alias. No build was needed.

1. Deleted the read, `if (!answer.success) onOutcome({ kind: 'partial', answer });`. Anchor 1 to 0. Result: `3 failed | 1 passed`. The three partial-answer pins went red; the throw pin stayed green.
2. Made the History reload clear the undo slot too (`setLoading(true); setUndoOutcome(null); setError(null);`), which is the base mechanism. Anchor 1 to 0. Result: `3 failed | 1 passed`. The three History pins went red; the cancelled-screen pin stayed green. The first attempt at this leg was refused by the tool before any test ran, because the replacement contained the anchor. It is declared here and was not counted.

### Reverse type check

A probe under `packages/plugin-grid/src`, type-checked through the rebuilt `packages/types/dist`, now refuses both old-shape literals. The old hand shape without `failures` gives `TS2741 Property 'failures' is missing`. An `action: 'update'` gives `TS2322 Type '"update"' is not assignable to type '"delete" | "restore"'`. The probe was removed.

## Gates (local, at `13af833`, each exit captured before any pipe)

- Build: turbo over the closure of `@object-ui/plugin-grid` and `@object-ui/data-objectstack`, plus `@object-ui/types` (concurrency 2). Exit 0, 13 tasks.
- `type-check`: `@object-ui/types` exit 0, `@object-ui/plugin-grid` exit 0, `@object-ui/data-objectstack` exit 0. The last is the downstream sweep: the consumers that name `ImportJobUndoResult`.
  - `plugin-grid`'s `tsconfig.test.json` program contains the new test file (`--listFiles`: 1 hit). It reads `packages/types/dist/data.d.ts`.
  - `@object-ui/app-shell` names only `undoImportJob: undefined`, an optional method whose type did not change. It is declared to CI.
- `lint`: `@object-ui/plugin-grid` exit 0 (0 errors), `@object-ui/types` exit 0 (0 errors). The warnings predate this branch.
- `pnpm check:i18n-keys` 0 · `check:i18n-drift` 0 (0 en values changed, 3 keys added) · `check:i18n-dead-keys` 0 (the new keys are not listed).
- `pnpm check:spec-symbols` 0 · `check:spec-floors` 1 (whole repo; `@object-ui/types` 0 findings, as above).
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations` 0 (`0 new citation(s)`) · `check:control-bytes` 0.
- `check-changeset-presence` 0 · `check-changeset-no-major` 0 · `check-changeset-fixed` 0.
- `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over the 15 changed paths: `NOT GOVERNED`.
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline` 0 (`Lockfile is up to date`): the floor move leaves the lockfile valid.
- The full farm is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- **Docs.** No page under `content/docs/**` or any package README describes the import undo today. This claim's file surface does not cover docs, so none was added; that is noted here and not filed.
- **Record ids are not shown.** Each `failures` entry also carries `id`, `action` and `code`. The notice shows the refusal sentence the card asks for, not the opaque record id.
